theme: Defilement; Peter’s confession; the cross predicted
readingInstruction: Read Matthew 15:1-16:28. Jesus teaches what really defiles a person, heals a Gentile woman’s daughter, feeds four thousand, and asks the disciples who they say he is. Peter’s confession is the center of the Gospel. Read 16:13-28 slowly.
settingTheScene: The conflict with the Pharisees continues. Jesus turns away from the hand-washing traditions to the heart. He then travels into Gentile territory, where he meets a woman of great faith. Then, in the region of Caesarea Philippi, he asks the question that changes everything. From that point on, Matthew says, Jesus begins to show the disciples that he must go to Jerusalem and suffer.
observation: “This people honors me with their lips, but their heart is far from me” (15:8).
“What comes out of the mouth proceeds from the heart, and this defiles a person” (15:18).
“Woman, great is your faith! Be it done for you as you desire” (15:28).
“Beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees” (16:6).
“Who do you say that I am?” (16:15).
“You are the Christ, the Son of the living God” (16:16).
“And I tell you, you are Peter, and on this rock I will build my church, and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it” (16:18).
“If anyone would come after me, let him deny himself and take up his cross and follow me” (16:24).
interpretation:
Jesus says that defilement is not about unwashed hands or food. It is about the heart. Evil thoughts, murder, adultery, theft, and slander all come from within. This was shocking to people who defined holiness by external rules. The real problem is inside, and only God can change it.

The Canaanite woman is a surprising example of faith. She is a Gentile who cries out to the Son of David. Jesus tests her, and she persists with humility: even dogs eat the crumbs from the table. Jesus commends her: “Great is your faith!” A foreigner understands what the leaders of Israel do not.

Then comes the pivot. Jesus asks who people say he is, and then, “Who do you say that I am?” Peter answers, “You are the Christ, the Son of the living God.” This is the memory verse of the unit. Christ means the Messiah, the anointed king. Jesus says that this was revealed to Peter by the Father. On this confession, Jesus will build his church, and not even death’s gates will stand against it. Whether “the rock” refers to Peter, to his confession, or both, the church rests on the truth that Jesus is the Christ.

But immediately Jesus begins to explain that the Christ must suffer, be killed, and be raised. Peter rebukes him, and Jesus calls him Satan, a stumbling block, for setting his mind on the things of man. Then the call goes out to all: deny yourself, take up your cross, and follow. “Whoever loses his life for my sake will find it.” The Christ is a crucified Christ, and his followers walk the same road.
connection: Isaiah 29:13 is quoted in 15:8. Mark 7:14-23 adds that Jesus declared all foods clean. Romans 10:9 says if you confess with your mouth that Jesus is Lord and believe in your heart that God raised him, you will be saved. Ephesians 2:20 says the household of God is built on the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Christ Jesus himself being the cornerstone. Galatians 2:20: “I have been crucified with Christ.” Luke 9:23 adds “daily.” Hebrews 12:2.
application:
Answer Jesus’ question in your own words: “Who do you say that I am?” Write it down.

Ask where your heart is far from God while your lips are near. Bring that to him.

Think about what taking up your cross looks like in your current season.
prayerPrompts: Confess with Peter who you believe Jesus is.
Ask him to cleanse your heart from the inside.
Ask him to teach you what it means to take up your cross.
